hypotheses.interpretation: D5 changes from bridge gate to hearth corner; F5 changes from approach to chosen boundary after an actual collision. Appreciation and a short elective act are supported separately from permanent safety or long-game appetite.

hypotheses.claim: A continuing counterpart automatically creates continued player purpose.
support: Amber makes actual structures and announces actions.
A boundary blocks its next attempted entry in an unexperienced checked branch.
counterevidence: Player stops before the announced next action.
No desire for general expansion or conquest.
Remembered footprint ownership does not guarantee the original circuit remains alive.
hypotheses.interpretation: Keep the real counterpart and local history. A completed personal project is a valid ending; making the rival more relentless would not establish a wanted next creation.

nextExperiment.proposal: Test an established creation becoming material or catalyst for a different kind of construction, preserving its actual properties and history.
because: A place changing role was valued
The player preferred a small meaningful boundary to broader reach
The current expansion invitation did not supply further purpose
nextExperiment.prediction: After a valid ending, the player can name a new capability or relationship they want to construct with the existing creation, then actually begin it.
nextExperiment.limitations: A new scale must change what can be done, not act as a level-unlock token or another list of assigned targets. The original quiet ending remains valid.

priorDesignerProposal: After freezing inspectable laws, run an actual mandated long diagnostic and a separate elective-interest condition; permit early stopping, retain identities and test changing roles rather than a turn quota.
limits: AI report and elective behavior do not establish human enjoyment.
Narrative/aesthetic value is recorded as a player account; no mechanical frontier can verify it.
No overall enjoyment verdict follows from passing the safeguards. The independent critic must inspect the proposed and observed experience.
